# n8n-nodes-ibm-quantum: complete reference for AI assistants

This file is the machine-oriented reference for the `n8n-nodes-ibm-quantum` package: every node,
operation, parameter (with its internal name), output shape and known hardware pitfall, stated
plainly so an LLM can configure the nodes or generate n8n workflow JSON without guessing.
It is generated from the source of version 0.6.0. The human-oriented documentation is README.md;
release history is CHANGELOG.md.

Unofficial, community-maintained package. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by IBM.

## Package facts

- npm package: `n8n-nodes-ibm-quantum` (verified n8n community node; installable on n8n Cloud and
  self-hosted n8n via Settings, Community nodes).
- Purpose: build, run and retrieve quantum circuits on the IBM Quantum Platform (IBM Cloud) from
  n8n, via the Qiskit Runtime REST API. IBM renamed the service "IBM Quantum Compute Service" in
  July 2026; the endpoints, headers and payloads are unchanged.
- Zero runtime dependencies. No Qiskit, no Python. Circuits travel as OpenQASM 3 strings, or as
  base64 QPY when you have Qiskit available to produce it.
- Requires Node.js 24 on the n8n host when n8n is 2.36 or later, which is n8n's own engines
  requirement since 2.36.0 (August 2026); Node.js 22 (22.22 or newer) is enough only for n8n 2.35
  and older. The package's own `engines.node` is `>=22`, so it installs on either. Targets the
  current IBM Quantum Platform (quantum.cloud.ibm.com), NOT the retired legacy platform
  (api.quantum-computing.ibm.com).
- Repository: https://github.com/TuguiDragos/n8n-nodes-ibm-quantum

## The 3 nodes

n8n workflow JSON uses these exact `type` strings (community packages prefix the package name):

| node (UI display name) | type string | kind |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| IBM Quantum (Unofficial) | `n8n-nodes-ibm-quantum.ibmQuantum` | action node, all operations |
| IBM Quantum (Unofficial) Trigger | `n8n-nodes-ibm-quantum.ibmQuantumTrigger` | polling trigger, fires when a job reaches a terminal state, carrying the failure reason when there is one |
| IBM Quantum Error (Unofficial) Trigger | `n8n-nodes-ibm-quantum.ibmQuantumErrorTrigger` | retired, hidden from the node panel; still installed so existing workflows keep running. For NEW workflows use the trigger above with `statusFilter: failedOrCanceled`, but do not migrate an existing one without rewriting its expressions: the output shape differs, see below |

The action node is on `typeVersion: 2`; use that for anything new. Version 1 still loads unchanged,
and differs in exactly one parameter: the session mode is `mode` on version 1 and `sessionMode` on
version 2. Both triggers are `typeVersion: 1`. All three require the `ibmQuantumApi` credential.
The action node has one main input and one main output; the triggers have no input and one output.

Only the action node is exposed as an AI Agent tool. The triggers deliberately are not: a polling
trigger cannot be invoked by an agent, and the n8n verification ruleset rejects the property on
trigger nodes.

## Credential: `ibmQuantumApi` (display name "IBM Quantum API")

| field (internal name) | type | default | meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `apiKey` | string (password) | none | IBM Cloud API key from https://cloud.ibm.com/iam/apikeys. Exchanged automatically for a short-lived IAM bearer token (POST https://iam.cloud.ibm.com/identity/token, grant type `urn:ibm:params:oauth:grant-type:apikey`). n8n caches the token and refreshes it on 401. |
| `instanceCrn` | string | none | Cloud Resource Name of the Qiskit Runtime instance, from https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/instances. Starts with `crn:v1`. Sent as the `Service-CRN` header on every request, and it is the instance `setCostLimit` changes unless that operation's own `instanceCrn` parameter is set. Its seventh colon-separated field, `a/<account id>`, is the account id `getAccountConfiguration` sends to `GET /accounts/{id}`; no other endpoint returns it. |
| `region` | options: `us-east`, `eu-de` | `us-east` | Must match the region the instance was created in. Picks the API host: `us-east` maps to `https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/api/v1`, `eu-de` maps to `https://eu-de.quantum.cloud.ibm.com/api/v1`. A mismatch yields HTTP 404 with `code 1279`, naming the CRN: "Instance crn:... not found", plus a solution paragraph. Authentication is NOT the problem in that case: measured by calling the eu-de host with a us-east CRN, `GET /versions` still answered 200 with seven versions while every instance-scoped endpoint 404'd, so the IAM token carries across regions and only the instance is regional. These are the only two regions IBM operates. |
| `apiVersion` | string | `2026-04-15` | Date sent as the `IBM-API-Version` header; selects the response schema. |

The credential ships a connection test (GET `/backends`) that validates all four fields at once.
There is also a hidden `sessionToken` field the token exchange fills in; never set it manually.

**API version validation.** The node checks this field before every run. A value that is not a real
YYYY-MM-DD date (including an empty one, or an impossible date like 2026-02-31) fails locally with a
clear message, because IBM would otherwise reject the request with an error naming neither the field
nor the cause. A well-formed date older than `2026-04-15` is accepted and logged as a warning: those
versions still answer today. As of August 2026, `2026-04-15` is the only version IBM does not list
as deprecated, and every earlier one has a published sunset during 2027.

## Action node: resources and operations

Top-level parameters on every action node: `resource` (default `job`) and `operation`. Six
resources: `account`, `backend`, `circuit`, `job`, `session`, `workload`. An unknown resource or
operation fails with a clear error rather than falling through to another handler.

Parameter names below are the internal names used in workflow JSON. "raw IBM body" means the API
response is passed through unchanged.

### Resource: `account`

| operation | HTTP call | parameters | output |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `getUsage` (default) | GET /instances/usage | none | raw IBM body: period usage, e.g. `usage_consumed_seconds`, `usage_limit_seconds` |
| `getInstance` | GET /instance | none | raw IBM body: instance details (plan, CRN, name) |
| `getConfiguration` | GET /instances/configuration | none | raw IBM body: instance configuration, including the cost limit |
| `getAccountConfiguration` | GET /accounts/{id} | `planId` (string, optional; trimmed and sent as `plan_id` when non-empty, at most 64 characters, a number from an expression is sent as text and a value that is neither text nor a number counts as empty) | raw IBM body: `{ plans: [{ plan_id, subscription_id, subscription_name, usage_allocation_seconds, usage_limit_seconds, unallocated_usage_seconds, backends[], max_ttl, active_ttl, interactive_ttl, start_time, end_time, functions[], custom_functions }] }`, one entry per plan on the account, or the one plan asked for. The account id is not a parameter: the node reads it from the credential's `instanceCrn` (the `a/<account id>` field). A CRN without that field, or with an id outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}`, fails locally before any request: the message names the credential's Instance CRN, except for the ids the shared identifier guard rejects first (whitespace only, dots only, an unpaired surrogate, over 1000 characters), whose messages name Account ID, a parameter this node deliberately does not have. |
| `getManyInstances` | GET https://resource-controller.cloud.ibm.com/v2/resource_instances?resource_id=b6049020-80f4-11eb-a0f7-e35ec9b4054f | `returnAll` (boolean, default false), `limit` (number, default 50, max 100; a value below 1 or unreadable falls back to 50; ignored when `returnAll` is true), `plan` (options: `` (Any, default), `flex`, `open`, `pay-as-you-go`, `premium`; mapped to IBM's `resource_plan_id`) | with `returnAll` off, the raw Resource Controller body `{ rows_count, next_url, resources[] }`; each resource has `crn`, `guid`, `name`, `region_id`, `resource_plan_id`, `state` and `extensions: { instance_limit_seconds, usage_allocation_seconds, backends }` (`["ANY"]` means every backend on the plan). With `returnAll` on the body is synthesized instead: the node follows `next_url` up to 20 pages of 100 and returns `{ resources, rows_count, next_url, truncated }`, `next_url` empty and `truncated` false when the listing was exhausted. |
| `setCostLimit` | PATCH https://resource-controller.cloud.ibm.com/v2/resource_instances/{crn URL-encoded} | `clearLimit` (boolean, default false; when true the limit is removed and `instanceLimit` is ignored), `instanceLimit` (number, default 600; an integer of at least 1 when `clearLimit` is false, anything else fails before the request), `instanceCrn` (string, default empty = the credential's instance; any value must start with `crn:v1:`) | the Resource Controller's updated instance body plus `instanceLimitSeconds`: `extensions.instance_limit_seconds` read back from the response: the limit in force. After a clear it is not null but the plan's own default, 600 on the Open plan, measured on 2026-09-10 with `response.parameters.instance_limit_seconds` null in the same body; null appears only when IBM reports no limit at all. The body sent is `{ "parameters": { "timestamp": "<now, ISO 8601>", "instance_limit_seconds": <int or null> } }`; only those two keys, so `usage_allocation_seconds` and `backends` stay unchanged. |
| `getAnalytics` | GET /analytics/usage | `analyticsFilters` | raw IBM body: usage totals. Every usage and queue-time figure is in MILLISECONDS (the spec says so on each field), unlike `getUsage` and `getMetrics`, which report seconds. |
| `getAnalyticsGrouped` | GET /analytics/usage_grouped | `analyticsFilters`, `groupBy` | raw IBM body: usage grouped by the chosen key, in milliseconds |
| `getAnalyticsByDate` | GET /analytics/usage_grouped_by_date | `analyticsFilters` | raw IBM body: a usage time series, in milliseconds. The API requires `group_by`, and accepts only `instance`, so the node always sends that. |
| `getAnalyticsFilters` | GET /analytics/filters | none | raw IBM body: the filter values this caller may use |
| `getApiVersions` | GET /versions | none | raw IBM body: `{ versions: [{ version, status, sunset_date? }] }`. Use it to confirm which `IBM-API-Version` dates are still live before changing the credential. |

`groupBy` options: `backend` (default), `instance`, `plan`, `subscription_id`, `user_id`.

`analyticsFilters` collection keys: `backend`, `instance`, `plan`, `subscriptionId`, `userId` (each
comma-separated for several values, sent as repeated query keys), `intervalStart` and `intervalEnd`
(dateTime, the reporting window), and `simulators` (boolean, default true; only the opt-out is sent
because the API already defaults to true. IBM retired its cloud simulators on 15 May 2024 and still
accepts the filter, so for usage since then it changes nothing).

`setCostLimit` writes the instance cost limit through the IBM Cloud Resource Controller, the
replacement IBM's spec names for the deprecated `PUT /instances/configuration` (which hung for 180
seconds and was dropped in 0.5.0). Facts an assistant needs: the request needs the same IAM bearer
token and nothing else, but the node's credential adds `Service-CRN` and `IBM-API-Version` to every
signed request, so both reach the Resource Controller too, where they are undefined; measured on
2026-09-07, the Resource Controller tolerates them, answering both calls as documented with the
headers present. The `timestamp` inside `parameters` is
required because IBM silently ignores a `parameters` object identical to the previous request; the
node sets it to the current time on every write. Read `extensions`, not `parameters`, when checking
what is in force: `parameters` only echoes the last request. Removing a cap takes the `clearLimit`
switch, and what it leaves in force is the plan's default, not no limit: measured on the Open plan,
a clear sent `instance_limit_seconds: null`, the response echoed that null under `parameters`, and
`extensions` reported 600, so `instanceLimitSeconds` read 600. Never a zero: a Cost Limit that is not a whole number of at least 1 fails before the
request, so an expression that resolves to nothing cannot clear the cap by accident. Which IBM
Cloud platform role the write requires has not been verified; IBM's cost guide says only
administrators and owners can edit an instance. The Resource Controller path has not been exercised
from this project against a live account (the 0.4.1 verification covered the old endpoint only), so
treat the first write as a test and confirm with `getManyInstances`. A limit that is reached
cancels running jobs with status Cancelled and reason "Ran too long"; queued jobs stay queued.

`getAccountConfiguration` is the account-wide read. `getUsage`, `getInstance` and `getConfiguration`
describe the one instance the credential's CRN names; `/accounts/{id}` lists every plan on that
account with its limits, allocation, allowed backends, session TTL caps and functions, and answers
the default configuration when IBM holds none. `plan_id` values are Global Catalog plan ids, the
identifier `getInstance` returns as `plan_id` (the Open plan is
`850b21a7-71de-4e53-9441-1abdd202f35d`). That the two endpoints report the same identifier form is
read from the spec, which describes both as defined in Global Catalog, and not yet confirmed live.

### Resource: `backend`

| operation | parameters | output |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `list` (default) | none | raw IBM body: `{ devices: [ { name, qubits, is_simulator, status: { name }, queue_length, ... } ] }`. `is_simulator` is deprecated by IBM (every device is real hardware; the field is due for removal). |
| `getConfiguration` | `backendName` (string, required), `calibrationId` (string, default `''`; sent as the query parameter `calibration_id`, at most 100 characters, empty omits it) | raw IBM body; includes `basis_gates` (the native gate set) and the coupling map, for the current calibration or for the one named |
| `getDefaults` | `backendName` (string, required) | raw IBM body in principle, but in practice always empty: IBM answers with the literal `null`, content-length 4, which the node reports as `{}` rather than passing a null item into the workflow. Measured on all three devices this account can reach (ibm_fez, ibm_kingston, ibm_marrakesh) and confirmed outside the node with a direct HTTP call, against 607338 bytes from `getProperties` on the same backend. |
| `getProperties` | `backendName` (string, required), `calibrationId` (string, default `''`; sent as `calibration_id`, at most 100 characters, empty omits it), `updatedBefore` (dateTime, default `''`; sent as `updated_before`, IBM returns the properties whose `last_update_date` is before it; refused locally unless it parses as a date and time) | raw IBM body: calibration data (T1/T2, gate errors, readout errors) |
| `getStatus` | `backendName` (string, required) | raw IBM body: operational state and queue length |
| `getLeastBusy` | `minQubits` (number, default 0; 0 disables the filter), `includeSimulators` (boolean, default false; deprecated: it keeps devices flagged `is_simulator: true`, of which there are none since IBM retired its cloud simulators on 15 May 2024, so it changes nothing), `rankBy` (options, default `queueLength`; `waitAverage`, `waitP50` and `waitP95` sort by IBM's `wait_time_seconds.average`, `.p50` and `.p95`; a device without the figure sorts last; ties fall back to queue length), `processorFamily` (string, default empty meaning any family; compared case-insensitively with `processor_type.family`, for example `Heron` or `Nighthawk`; a device reporting no family is dropped while the filter is set) | `{ leastBusy: string\|null, queueLength: number\|null, waitTimeSeconds: { average, p50, p95 }\|null, candidates: [{ name, queueLength, qubits, status, family, revision, waitTimeSeconds }] }` |

Every backend parameter (`backendName`, `backend` on submit, `sessionBackend`, and the backend
filters on the job and workload listings) is an options field backed by the `getBackends`
loadOptions method, which reads `GET /v1/backends` and labels each entry with its processor family
and revision when IBM reports them, its status and its queue depth, for example
`ibm_fez (Heron r2, online, 7 queued)`. The stored value is the bare backend name, so a workflow
written before this existed is unaffected, and any value starting with `=` is an expression that
n8n exempts from option validation. The list refreshes when the node is opened and on Refresh List,
never on a timer.

`getLeastBusy` is computed client-side from `GET /v1/backends?fields=wait_time_seconds`: it keeps
devices whose status is `online`, drops devices smaller than `minQubits` or with an unknown qubit
count, drops devices whose `processor_type.family` does not equal `processorFamily`
case-insensitively while that filter is set (a device reporting no family is dropped too), and drops
any device still flagged `is_simulator: true` unless `includeSimulators` is on (a check that matches
nothing today and keeps every device once IBM removes the deprecated field), then sorts by the
`rankBy` metric: `queueLength` (the default) uses `queue_length`; `waitAverage`, `waitP50` and
`waitP95` use IBM's `wait_time_seconds` (`average`, `p50`, `p95`, integers in seconds that IBM
computes per device). A device without the chosen figure sorts last, ties fall back to queue length,
and remaining ties keep IBM's order. `leastBusy` is the winning device's `name`, and `null` when
nothing qualifies or the winner carries no readable one, so handle that case; `waitTimeSeconds` is
`null` on any device IBM returned no figure for, and each of its three fields is `null` individually
when missing; `qubits` is `null` on a candidate IBM reports no count for, which its schema allows by
declaring that field nullable and leaving it out of the required list. Every key of the shape is
emitted, carrying `null` where IBM reported nothing, so a workflow tests for `null` and never for a
key that is not there. A `rankBy` that carries a value outside the four fails the item with "Rank
By must be one of queueLength, waitAverage, waitP50, waitP95." (an expression resolving to nothing
keeps the default instead) and a `processorFamily` that is not text (an array or object from an
expression) fails with "Processor Family must be text such as Heron or Nighthawk, or empty for any
family."; both are checked before the request. A `devices` key that is not an array, and an entry
inside it that is not an object, rank as nothing rather than failing the item, so a body the node
cannot read answers `leastBusy: null` with an empty `candidates`.

### Resource: `circuit`

Both circuit operations are local; they make no API call and need no credential values.

`build` (default) parameters:
- `numQubits` (number, required, default 2): quantum register size, min 1.
- `numClbits` (number, default 2): classical register size, min 0.
- `circuitParameters` (string, default empty): comma-separated names of symbolic angles, e.g.
  `theta,phi`. Each becomes an `input float[64] name;` declaration and may be used in place of a
  number in any gate's `params`. A name must be an OpenQASM 3 identifier, not a keyword, constant,
  gate name or one of the registers `q` and `c`, and not repeated. `p0`, `_gate_q_0` and `_gate_q_1`
  are refused as well, even when the circuit has no `rzz`: they are the names inside the `rzz`
  definition the builder writes. Bind them at submit time through the Sampler or Estimator
  `parameters` field, as an object: `{"theta": 1.5708, "phi": 0.5}`. Use the object form whenever
  more than one name is declared: a positional array is NOT bound in declaration order, because
  Qiskit's OpenQASM 3 importer returns the parameters sorted by name, so `[1.5708, 0.5]` on
  `theta,phi` gives `phi` the first value. `parameterNames` in the output is the declaration order,
  the order of the `input` lines.
- `gates` (fixedCollection, entries under key `gate`, ordered): each entry has
  - `gate` (options, default `h`): one of the palette gates below, `rzz` and `delay` included since
    0.6.0.
  - `qubits` (string, required): comma-separated qubit indices, e.g. `0` or `0,1`. For controlled
    gates the control comes FIRST and the target LAST (`0,1` means control 0, target 1). Toffoli
    takes `control,control,target`. Empty is allowed only for a full-width barrier.
  - `params` (string, only for `rx`,`ry`,`rz`,`rzz`,`p`,`crx`,`cry`,`crz`,`u`): comma-separated
    angles in radians, or names declared in `circuitParameters`. One value for R, RZZ and Phase
    gates; exactly three (theta, phi, lambda) for `u`. A name that was not declared is refused at
    build time.
  - `clbit` (number, only for `measure`, default 0): target classical bit.
  - `duration` (string, only for `delay`, required): a number followed by `ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s` or
    `dt`, e.g. `100ns` or `160dt`, no space; a `dt` count must be a whole number.

Output: `{ qasm3: string, numQubits, numClbits, gateCount, instructionCount }`. `gateCount` is the
number of rows in the gate list; `instructionCount` is the number of instruction lines written to
`qasm3`, lower by one for every `id`, which is validated and then dropped (see the palette table).
`parameterNames` (string[]) is added only when `circuitParameters` is non-empty, in declaration
order. The `gate rzz` block and the `input` declarations are header lines and are not counted in
`instructionCount`; a `delay` row is.

All input is validated at build time (wrong arity, out-of-range index, non-numeric value, measure
past the classical register, invalid register sizes) and fails with a message naming the gate.
A multi-qubit gate must also use DISTINCT qubit indices: `cx` with `0,0` is refused locally, because
IBM queues such a program and only then fails it with reason code 1603 ("duplicate bit arguments").
`barrier` is exempt, a repeated index there is harmless. Register sizes are capped at 4096, far above
any real device, to stop a runaway expression emitting a register no backend can accept. An
expression that sets `gates` to something other than a collection object, the entry list on its own
included, or its `gate` key to something other than a list of entries, builds a circuit with no
gates rather than failing the item; an entry inside the list that is not an object is refused by its
gate number like any other unusable row.

`import` parameters: `qasm3Input` (string, required). Validates the program starts with an
OpenQASM 3 version header (`OPENQASM 3.0;`) and passes it through. Output: `{ qasm3: string }`.
This operation is OpenQASM 3 only; to submit QPY, paste it straight into the submit operation.

### Resource: `job`

3 programs submit a job: `submitSampler` (the default), `submitEstimator` and
`submitNoiseLearner`. They share the job envelope described first, then differ.

Shared by all three:

| parameter | type | default | notes |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `backend` | string, required | none | Device that runs the circuit. The circuit must already be ISA (transpiled) for THIS backend; see "Hardware reality" below. |
| `circuitFormat` | options `qasm3` or `qpy` | `qasm3` | Which field below carries the circuit. A workflow saved before this parameter existed has no value stored and behaves as `qasm3`, as does an expression that resolves to nothing. Any other value is refused before the request, naming the field and the two spellings; without that guard it fell through to the OpenQASM field, which n8n does not display for it, and the run failed on n8n's own `Could not get parameter "qasm3"`. |
| `qasm3` | string OR array of strings, required when format is `qasm3` | none | The OpenQASM 3 circuit. Typically an expression, e.g. `={{ $('Build').item.json.qasm3 }}`. Must start with an `OPENQASM 3` header or the node rejects it locally, before any quota is spent. **An expression resolving to an ARRAY submits every circuit in one job**, one PUB each, sharing the same `shots`, `parameters`, `observables` and `precision`. A job carries about 2 QPU seconds of fixed overhead regardless of its circuits, measured repeatedly on ibm_fez, so a batch of 5 costs that once instead of five times. Every entry is validated; the node sends at most 100 in one job, its own bound rather than IBM's. An empty array is refused. |
| `qpyCircuit` | string OR array of strings, required when format is `qpy` | none | The circuit as QPY that is **zlib compressed and then base64 encoded**. IBM decompresses on arrival, so base64 of the raw QPY bytes is rejected: submitting that live failed with reason code 1603, IBM having tried to read the base64 text as QASM. The node validates a real zlib header locally (first byte 0x78, header divisible by 31) and sends the value inside the wrapper the official client uses, `{"__type__": "QuantumCircuit", "__value__": <value>}`, rather than as a bare string. Produce it in Python with `qiskit.qpy.dump(circuit, buffer)` then `base64.b64encode(zlib.compress(buffer.getvalue()))`. Accepts an array on the same terms as `qasm3`; each entry is wrapped separately. |
| `logLevel` | options `''`, `critical`, `error`, `warning`, `info`, `debug` | `''` | Sent as `log_level`; raises the verbosity IBM records, readable later with Get Logs. Omitted when empty. |
| `submitSessionId` | string | `''` | Session or batch ID from Session Create; runs the job inside that reservation. Sent as top-level `session_id`. |
| `submitCalibrationId` | string | `''` | Sent as top-level `calibration_id`, beside `session_id`, never inside `params`. Names the calibration the job should run with; IBM's schema allows 1 to 100 characters and the node refuses a longer value locally. Empty omits the field. The job reports the calibration it actually used as `calibration_id` in the submit response and in Get Status. Whether IBM honours a calibration that is no longer current, or what it answers for one it does not know, is unverified: no live job has been submitted with the field set. |
| `maxCost` | number | 0 | Maximum runtime seconds before IBM cancels the job, sent as `cost`. IBM allows at most 10800 (3 hours) and the node clamps to that. Zero omits the field, and IBM then stamps the job with the plan maximum, verified live as the Open plan's entire 600 second allowance for the 28 day window. Set a real number to stop one runaway job from spending all of it. |
| `jobTags` | string OR array of strings | `''` | Comma-separated tags stored on the job (max 8); an array is read one tag per entry, commas and all, and an entry that is blank, or that is neither text nor a number, fails the item instead of being dropped. The practical way to find jobs again: filter on them in Job Get Many, Workload Get Many and both triggers. |
| `privateJob` | boolean | false | Marks the job private (inputs and results hidden from other collaborators). IBM's spec: the inputs are deleted once the job completes and the results once they have been read, so Get Results carries a private job's shots exactly once and a second read answers empty. Needs a plan that supports private jobs. |
| `additionalOptions` | json | `{}` | Escape hatch merged into the job's `options` object: the primitive options for Sampler and Estimator, the learner options for the noise learner. For example `{"execution": {"rep_delay": 0.00025}}`. Must be a JSON object. Its top-level keys are validated locally against IBM's schema for the chosen program, and an unknown key is refused before the request with a message naming the key and the allowed keys. Sampler accepts `default_shots`, `dynamical_decoupling`, `execution`, `experimental`, `simulator`, `twirling`; Estimator accepts those plus `default_precision`, `resilience`, `seed_estimator`; the noise learner accepts `experimental`, `layer_pair_depths`, `max_layers_to_learn`, `num_randomizations`, `shots_per_randomization`, `simulator`, `support_qiskit`, `twirling_strategy`. There is no `environment` key: the Python client's `log_level`, `job_tags` and `private` are `logLevel`, `jobTags` and `privateJob` above. Nested keys are left to IBM. Dedicated fields win over keys repeated here, key by key: `shots` travels with the circuit and overrides `default_shots`, the three suppression toggles overwrite their own keys, and every entry of the option collections below overwrites the same key inside this JSON while leaving sibling keys alone. |

Sampler and Estimator only. The noise learner takes bare circuits rather than PUBs, so it has no
parameter bindings, and its options object is declared `additionalProperties: false`, so the three
error-suppression toggles below, and the option collections beside them, are never merged into it:

| parameter | type | default | notes |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `parameters` | json | `{}` | Bindings for a parametrized circuit: either a JSON object mapping parameter names to values or arrays, e.g. `{"theta": 1.5708}`, or a bare array of values, e.g. `[3.14159]`. Both shapes were verified live on a circuit with one parameter and return the same counts. An array is positional against the parameters sorted by name, which is the order Qiskit's OpenQASM 3 importer returns them in and not the order the program declares them, so use the object form for a circuit with more than one parameter. Empty string or `{}` means no bindings. |
| `dynamicalDecoupling` | boolean | false | Sends `options.dynamical_decoupling.enable = true`. Safe on any circuit. |
| `twirlingGates` | boolean | false | Sends `options.twirling.enable_gates = true`. MUST stay off for circuits containing fractional gates (a parametrised `rx` or `rzz`, which includes anything Qiskit transpiles for a Heron processor); IBM fails the job with "gate twirling does not support fractional gates". |
| `twirlingMeasure` | boolean | false | Sends `options.twirling.enable_measure = true`. No fractional-gate restriction. |
| `dynamicalDecouplingOptions` | collection | `{}` | Sent under `options.dynamical_decoupling`, only the entries added; they apply wherever dynamical decoupling is on (the toggle, or an `enable` written into `additionalOptions`). `sequenceType` (`XX`, `XpXm`, `XY4`, default XX) as `sequence_type`; `extraSlackDistribution` (`middle`, `edges`) as `extra_slack_distribution`; `schedulingMethod` (`alap`, `asap`) as `scheduling_method`; `skipResetQubits` (boolean, default true) as `skip_reset_qubits`. |
| `twirlingOptions` | collection | `{}` | Sent under `options.twirling`, only the entries added; refines the two twirling toggles. `numRandomizations` and `shotsPerRandomization` (text, default `auto`) as `num_randomizations` and `shots_per_randomization`: a whole number between 1 and 2147483647 or the literal `auto`; an empty value, and an expression that resolves to nothing, omit the key, while other text, a number outside that range, and anything else an expression hands over, such as null, a boolean or an object, are refused locally; `strategy` (`active`, `active-accum`, `active-circuit`, `all`, default active-accum). |
| `executionOptions` | collection | `{}` | Sent under `options.execution`, only the entries added. `initQubits` (boolean, default true) as `init_qubits`; `repDelay` (number of seconds, default 0.00025, refused below 0) as `rep_delay`; `measType` (`classified`, `kerneled`, `avg_kerneled`, default classified) as `meas_type`, Sampler only: the UI hides it for the Estimator and the node drops it from an Estimator request even when an expression supplies it. |

`submitSampler` only: `shots` (number, default 1024; a fraction is floored and a value below 1 or
unreadable falls back to 1024, the clamp convention the shots and limit fields follow; above
10000000 the item fails with "Shots is N; IBM accepts at most 10000000 per circuit." before any
request, which is the limit the service enforces rather than the int32 bound the spec declares).
`submitEstimator` only:
- `observables` (json, default `"ZZ"`): a Pauli string over letters I, X, Y, Z (one letter per
  qubit), an array of such strings, or a coefficient map like `{"ZI": 1.0, "IZ": 0.5}`. Letters are
  validated locally; length against qubit count is validated by IBM at submit time.
- `resilienceLevel` (options 0/1/2, default 1): error-mitigation level.
- `precision` (number, default 0): target precision; 0 means backend default.
- `defaultPrecision` (number, default 0): sent as `options.default_precision` when above 0; refused
  unless a number at least 0. `precision`, when set, overrides it for every PUB.
- `seedEstimator` (string, default `''`): sent as `options.seed_estimator`; a whole number between 0
  and 2147483647; other text and out-of-range numbers are refused, empty omits the key. Text rather
  than a number because 0 is a real seed.
- `resilienceOptions` (collection, default `{}`): sent under `options.resilience`, only the entries
  added, each winning over the same key in `additionalOptions`. `measureMitigation` (boolean,
  default true) as `measure_mitigation`; `zneMitigation` (boolean, default false) as
  `zne_mitigation`; `zneNoiseFactors` (comma-separated numbers, refused unless finite) as
  `zne.noise_factors`; `zneExtrapolator` (multi-select of `linear`, `exponential`,
  `double_exponential`, `polynomial_degree_1` to `polynomial_degree_7`, `fallback`; an expression may
  hand over a string or comma list) as `zne.extrapolator`; `zneAmplifier` (`gate_folding`,
  `gate_folding_front`, `gate_folding_back`, `pea`, default gate_folding) as `zne.amplifier`;
  `pecMitigation` (boolean, default false) as `pec_mitigation`; `pecMaxOverhead` (number, default
  100, refused below 0) as `pec.max_overhead`, where 0 is sent as `null` meaning no cap;
  `pecNoiseGain` (text, default `auto`) as `pec.noise_gain`, a number at least 0 or `auto`;
  `noiseLearningMaxLayers`, `noiseLearningRandomizations`, `noiseLearningShotsPerRandomization`
  (numbers, default 0, zero omits the key) as `layer_noise_learning.max_layers_to_learn`,
  `.num_randomizations`, `.shots_per_randomization`; `noiseLearningLayerPairDepths`
  (comma-separated whole numbers) as `layer_noise_learning.layer_pair_depths`.
  `measure_noise_learning`, `extrapolated_noise_factors`, `layer_noise_model`, `simulator` and
  `experimental` stay in `additionalOptions`. PEC, PEA and gate twirling are refused by IBM on
  circuits with fractional gates (error 1519).
- Wire example, Estimator: `options: { resilience: { zne_mitigation: true, zne: { noise_factors:
  [1, 3, 5], extrapolator: ['exponential', 'linear'] } }, seed_estimator: 7, default_precision:
  0.02 }`, with `resilience_level` still a sibling of `options` inside `params` and `precision`
  riding in each PUB as its fourth item.

Submit output: `{ jobId, backend, primitive, sessionId: string|null, warnings?, response }` where
`warnings` gathers whatever the submit checks found, so it can appear for a circuit that is wholly
in basis. The first check covers an OpenQASM 3 circuit using instructions outside the chosen
backend's `basis_gates`, read from `GET /backends/{name}/configuration` once per submit (no query
parameters), plus whatever the same configuration lists under `supported_instructions` (IBM puts
measure_2, if_else, store and the like there, and a Heron device with fractional gates off may list
rx and rzz only there), plus measure, reset, delay and barrier, which every device supports; the
warning names that backend and its `basis_gates` alone, for example `not in the ibm_miami basis
(cz, id, rz, sx, x)`. When the configuration cannot be read, is not an object, or carries no usable
`basis_gates`, the check falls back to the Heron union (cz, id, rx, rz, rzz, sx, x), ignores
`supported_instructions`, and the warning says `not in the IBM basis (cz, id, rx, rz, rzz, sx, x)`,
the 0.5.0 wording. Qiskit Runtime does not transpile, so such a job is accepted, queued and then
fails; the warning says so at submit time and never blocks the request. A second warning covers a
basis gate called without a definition: any gate the backend lists in `basis_gates` that
`stdgates.inc` does not define, which is `rzz` on every Heron device and, since 2026-09-10, `xslow`
on all three, is refused by IBM's importer when called bare, naming `gate 'rzz' is not defined` or
`gate 'xslow' is not defined`; the warning names the gate and the backend. Do not match on the
reason code: the identical program returned 1506 and 1603 on the same device thirteen hours apart,
so only the message is stable. Carrying Qiskit's own `gate rzz` block, the same circuit completes
and is not warned about, and a `gate xslow` definition silences the warning the same way. A third
warning covers an OpenQASM 3 circuit calling `id` in any operand form
(`id q[0];`, `id $0;`, `id qr[3];`): `id` is in the basis and `stdgates.inc` defines it, as
`U(0, 0, 0)`, yet a job carrying it failed on Heron with "the instruction u on qubits (n,) is not
supported" (measured for 0.3.3) even though IBM lists `id` as native; remove it, identity is a
no-op, and Circuit Build drops it for the same reason. Re-measured on 2026-09-07, IBM still fails
it with that message, so the warning stands; `id` stays in the basis because IBM still lists it.
A fourth warning covers `rzz` called with an angle outside `[0, pi/2]`, the only range IBM's
fractional `rzz` accepts: measured on `ibm_marrakesh` on 2026-09-10, a Grover circuit Qiskit had
transpiled against a bare `basis_gates` list carried `rzz(-1.5707963267948966)` and failed after
queueing with code 1517, "supported only for angles in the range [0, pi/2]". The scan reads an
angle written as a number or as `pi` scaled by a number (`-pi/2`, `3*pi/4`); a parameter name or
any other expression is left alone. A fifth warning covers a fractional gate, `rx` or `rzz`, in a
circuit submitted where gate twirling is on: through the Gate Twirling toggle or an `enable_gates`
in Additional Options, through Resilience Level 2 or PEC Mitigation, which IBM twirls itself, and
always through the noise learner, which learns by twirling. IBM refuses the combination after
queueing with code 1519, "Gate twirling does not support fractional gates", measured on
`ibm_marrakesh` on 2026-09-10 with an Estimator job at resilience 2 on an ansatz carrying `rx` and
a noise learner job on a layer carrying `rzz`; the warning names the gates and the twirling source.
A sixth check covers a two qubit gate landing on a pair the backend does not couple,
read from `coupling_map`: both gates can be perfectly in basis and it still fires. Operands are read
in two spellings, each with the index glued to the name: physical qubits (`$0`, what Qiskit's
exporter writes for a transpiled circuit) and indexed registers of any name (`q[0]`, `qr[3]`), with
a second quantum register offset by the sizes of the ones declared before it, the way IBM's importer
numbers qubits. `cz q [0], q [5];` and `cz $ 0, $ 5;` are read as nothing. Declarations are read
with any spaces or tabs around the size, on one line, and in the legacy spelling as well, so
`qubit [2] a;` and `qreg a[2];` offset what follows them exactly as `qubit[2] a;` does. Classical
bits are never read as qubits, in the same spellings: `bit[n] name;`, `bit [n] name;`,
`creg name[n];`. A size that is not a plain number is not read at all, so `qubit[N] a;` offsets
nothing and `bit[N] c;` is left looking like a quantum register. A `qubit` or `qreg` declaration
whose keyword, size and register name do not all sit on one line is read by neither reader, with the
same consequence; a `bit` or `creg` declaration needs only its keyword and name on one line, because
its reader never looks at the size.
The coupling warning names at most 20 pairs, each in its own sentence: an untranspiled circuit can
put a two qubit gate on every pair it touches, 4950 of them for 100 virtual qubits wired all to all,
of which ibm_fez does not couple 4839, so everything past the twentieth distinct pair becomes one
closing sentence counting what it did not name and saying to transpile. A pair counts once whichever
way round the circuit writes it, so `cz q[0], q[5]` and `cz q[5], q[0]` are one pair and one
sentence.
QPY is compressed, so it is not inspected. `response` is the raw IBM body. Submission returns
immediately; the job runs asynchronously, so pair it with `getResults` or the trigger node.

`submitNoiseLearner` only: `noiseLearnerOptions` (collection) with `maxLayersToLearn`,
`numRandomizations`, `shotsPerRandomization` (numbers; zero omits the field and leaves the choice
to IBM), `layerPairDepths` (comma-separated integers, sent as the array `layer_pair_depths`) and
`twirlingStrategy` (`active`, `active-accum`, `active-circuit`, `all`). The program characterises
the noise on the backend's entangling layers and returns learned Pauli-Lindblad error channels
rather than counts. Build its circuit with `numClbits: 0`: the learner does not measure the
circuit, and a classical register makes IBM reject anything that splits into more than one
entangling layer, with "ClassicalRegister with name 'c' appears in multiple layers with different
sizes". One layer survives, so this only appears once the circuit grows. The node emits a warning
when a line of the QASM it is handed starts with `bit[n]`, glued as Circuit Build writes it, and at
least two of its statements name two or more distinct qubits in the glued spelling the scanner
reads. Get Results parses those into
one `noiseLearner` pub per learned layer, and the full body stays in `raw`. Raising the
randomizations and shots is what makes a learning job expensive, which matters on the Open plan.

A QPY circuit is never sent as a plain string: wherever a PUB or `circuits` entry carries one, it
appears as `{"__type__": "QuantumCircuit", "__value__": "<base64 of zlib-compressed QPY>"}`.

Request body sent: `{ program_id: "sampler"|"estimator"|"noise-learner", backend, params: {...},
session_id?, calibration_id?, tags?, private?, cost?, log_level? }`. For Sampler and Estimator,
`params` is `{ version: 2, pubs: [pub, ...], options?, resilience_level? }` and the node submits one
PUB per circuit, so an array of circuits becomes an array of PUBs inside one job. `options` is
assembled from Additional Options first, then the option collections, then the three toggles and
the dedicated fields, each later source overwriting the same key from an earlier one while leaving
sibling keys alone, so a field always wins over the JSON; a key nobody set is absent, and an
all-empty configuration sends no `options` at all, exactly as before 0.6.0. Sampler PUB is
`[circuit, parameters, shots]`, Estimator PUB is `[circuit, observables, parameters?, precision?]`.
For the noise learner, `params` is `{ version: 2, circuits: [circuit], options? }`.

Other job operations:

| operation | parameters | output |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `getStatus` | `jobId` (required), `includeParams` (boolean, default true; false sends `exclude_params=true` and the body comes back without `params`, the submitted circuit) | raw IBM job body; status lives at `state.status` (e.g. `Queued`, `Running`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Cancelled`), failure details at `state.reason`, `state.reason_code`, `state.reason_solution` |
| `getResults` | `jobId` (required), `pollInterval` (seconds, default 5), `maxWait` (seconds, default 300), `registerName` (string, default '' meaning auto-detect) | see "Results format" below. BLOCKS the execution while polling, so prefer the trigger pattern for long hardware queues. Transient errors (429, 5xx, dropped connections) are retried until `maxWait`. Every poll sends `exclude_params=true`, so the `job` returned on timeout or failure carries no `params`; read the circuit back with `getStatus`. |
| `getLogs` | `jobId` | `{ jobId, logs }`. IBM sends the job log as `text/plain`, the node asks for the body as text, and `logs` is that text verbatim. It is a string in every case, including a log body that is itself valid JSON, so it can be split into lines without a type check. A job that logged nothing gives `''`. |
| `getMetrics` | `jobId` | raw IBM body: timestamps and usage, including `qpu_charge_time_seconds`. Note that `bss`, `usage.quantum_seconds` and `usage.seconds` were removed by IBM in API version 2026-03-15. |
| `list` (UI label "Get Many") | `returnAll` (boolean, default false), `limit` (default 50, max 200, IBM's hard cap; hidden in the UI and ignored when `returnAll` is true), `listFilters` (collection, below) | raw IBM body: `{ jobs: [...], count?, limit?, offset? }`, newest first by default. With `returnAll` true the node requests 200 jobs per page by offset, starting at `listFilters.offset`, until a page comes back short of 200 or the offset reaches the server's `count`, and returns `{ jobs: [every page merged, a job id repeated at a page boundary dropped], count?, limit?, offset: <start offset>, truncated?: true }`. `count` and `limit` are the server's values from the last page fetched; `truncated: true` is present only when the walk stopped at its cap of 50 pages (10,000 jobs). A failing page fails the item, nothing partial is returned. |
| `listTags` (UI label "Get Many Tags") | `tagSearch` (string, required, 3 to 100 characters) | raw IBM body: the tags in use on your jobs that contain the term. IBM has no way to list every tag: a term shorter than 3 characters is refused with a bare 400 naming neither the field nor the limit, so the node checks the bound locally first. `type=job` is always sent, being the only value the API accepts. |
| `updateTags` | `jobId`, `jobTags` | `{ jobId, tags }`. PUT replaces the FULL tag list; an empty input clears all tags, and an array carrying an entry that is blank, or that is neither text nor a number, is refused before the request rather than narrowed to the entries that could be read. Comma-separated text is not guarded that way: it still drops its empty entries, so `a,,b` sends two tags and a value that is nothing but separators clears the job. |
| `cancel` | `jobId` | `{ jobId, cancelled: true }` |
| `delete` | `jobId` | `{ jobId, deleted: true }` (permanent) |

`listFilters` collection keys: `backend` (string), `createdAfter` and `createdBefore` (dateTime),
`includeParams` (boolean, default false; set true to include each job's submitted circuit),
`offset` (number; jobs to skip, and with `returnAll` the offset the walk starts from),
`program` ('' | `sampler` | `estimator` | `noise-learner`, the `program_id` values Submit sends),
`sessionId` (string), `sort` (`desc` newest first | `asc`),
`pending` (`all` | `finished` | `pending`),
`tag` (comma-separated tags; a job must carry ALL of them; max 8).

### Resource: `workload`

One operation, `list`, shown in the UI as "Get Many" (GET /workloads). Lists jobs, sessions and batches together, which Job Get Many
cannot do. Parameters:

- `returnAll` (boolean, default false).
- `limit` (number, default 50, max 50; hidden in the UI and ignored when `returnAll` is true). Note
  this endpoint caps at 50, unlike Job Get Many which allows 200.
- `workloadFilters` collection: `backend` (string), `createdAfter` and `createdBefore` (dateTime),
  `next` and `previous` (the `nextCursor` and `previousCursor` values from a previous response;
  this listing pages by cursor, not by offset), `search` (free text matched against workload IDs
  and tags), `workloadMode` ('' | `job` | `session` | `batch`, sent as `mode`), `status`
  (multi-select of `pending`, `in_progress`, `failed`, `completed`, `canceled`), `tags`
  (comma-separated), `sort` (`-createdAt` newest first, the node's default, or `createdAt`).

The node always sends a sort value. Left alone, the API returns oldest first, which does not match
Job Get Many or the triggers, so the node asks for newest first unless you choose otherwise.

Output: the raw IBM body (`workloads`, `total_count`, `limit`, and the `next` and `previous` links
as `{ href }`), plus two keys the node adds: `nextCursor` and `previousCursor`, the `next` or
`previous` query parameter read out of the matching `href`, percent-decoded, or `null` when the
link is absent or carries no such parameter. Feed them back into `workloadFilters.next` and
`workloadFilters.previous`. The token format inside the link is IBM's own; measured on one account
it is base64 of a timestamp, and a token fed back returns the page it names.

With `returnAll` true the node asks for 50 workloads per page and follows `next.href`, sending its
`next` token back as the `next` query parameter with the same filters, until a page carries no such
token, the walk reaches its cap of 20 pages (1,000 workloads), or IBM repeats a token the walk has
already followed. The output is that same shape, built from the last page fetched, with `workloads`
holding every page merged in order and `truncated: true` present when the walk stopped short, which
covers both the cap and a repeated token; `nextCursor` then still names the page to carry on from.
An entry whose `id` has already been collected is dropped, so a workload appearing on two pages is
returned once; an entry carrying no `id` is always kept, since nothing identifies it as a repeat. A
failing page fails the item, nothing partial is returned.

### Resource: `session`

| operation | parameters | output |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `create` (default) | `sessionMode` on typeVersion 2 (`mode` on typeVersion 1): `batch` default or `dedicated`, and anything else is refused before the request naming both spellings, because IBM answers an unknown mode with a bare `Internal server error`; an expression that resolves to nothing keeps `batch`; `sessionBackend` (string, required); `maxTtl` (seconds, sent as `max_ttl`, default 28800; IBM caps it by plan, 600 on Open and 28800 on paid plans; non-positive omits the field and lets IBM apply the plan default) | `{ sessionId, mode, backend, response }`, where `mode` is the mode asked for and `response.mode` is IBM's own |
| `get` | `sessionId` (required) | raw IBM body |
| `setAccepting` | `sessionId`, `acceptingJobs` (boolean, default true) | `{ sessionId, acceptingJobs }`. Sending false ENDS the session, it does not pause it: IBM moves it to `state: "closed"` with `state_reason: "session_closed_early"` at once when nothing is running, and sending true afterwards flips `accepting_jobs` back without reopening it. |
| `close` | `sessionId` | `{ sessionId, closed: true }`. DELETE /sessions/{id}/close: the session stops accepting new jobs, queued jobs will not run, running jobs finish (the spec's wording; IBM's FAQ describes it as cancelling pending session jobs). `setAccepting` false instead lets queued jobs run before the session closes. |

Whatever the parameter is called in the UI, the value is always sent to IBM as `mode`.

`batch` queues jobs to run consecutively and is the ONLY mode the Open (free) plan allows.
`dedicated` reserves the QPU for low-latency back-to-back jobs (VQE and QAOA loops) and needs a paid
plan: on an Open instance IBM answers with error 1352, "You are not authorized to run a session
when using the {} plan", the braces standing for the plan name. Pass the returned `sessionId` into
each Submit's `submitSessionId`. Close the session when done so it stops holding the backend,
remembering that Close cancels queued jobs (see the table above) and that `setAccepting: false` is
the way to let them run first. IBM caps the TTL by plan: 10 minutes on the Open plan, 8 hours on
paid plans. The node's default of 28800 seconds is the paid-plan figure, so an Open batch ends
after 10 minutes whatever the field says. When the maximum TTL is reached IBM ends the workload and
any job still queued fails. A `dedicated` session that is opened and receives no job for 30 minutes
closes on its own. Both modes also carry an interactive TTL that cannot be configured: when it
passes with nothing queued the workload is deactivated rather than ended, and any later job
reactivates it until the maximum TTL. IBM documents that window as 1 minute for a batch on every
plan and 60 seconds for a session on the Premium plan, and says an instance may be configured with
a different value; Session Get reports the one in force as `interactive_ttl`, in seconds.

## Trigger nodes

Both are polling triggers: they run on the n8n scheduler (set the cadence with the built-in Poll
Times field) and only while the workflow is ACTIVE. Manual "Fetch Test Event" returns one matching
job without consuming state. On the very first poll they seed their cursor and emit nothing, so
pre-existing job history never fires the workflow. Each poll scans only finished jobs
(`pending=false`) without circuit payloads (`exclude_params=true`), remembers the last 500 seen job
IDs, and emits only jobs not seen before. `limit` is the size of the scan window: when more than
`limit` matching jobs finish between two polls, only the newest `limit` of them are emitted and
the rest never fire (measured on 2026-09-10: five jobs finishing inside one interval with
`limit: 2` fired the two newest).
The seen set is workflow static data, persisted by n8n: after an n8n restart the first poll fires
only the jobs that finished while n8n was down, once, and never the seeded history (measured on
2026-09-10 on n8n 2.38.6, and the same trigger on n8n 2.35.7 fired a new job exactly once).

`ibmQuantumTrigger` parameters:
- `statusFilter` (labelled Trigger On; options: `any` default meaning any terminal status,
  `completed`, `failed`, `canceled`, `failedOrCanceled` meaning failed or canceled but not
  completed): which terminal status fires.
- `limit` (number, default 50, max 200): jobs scanned per poll.
- `tagFilter` (string, default ''): comma-separated tags; only jobs carrying ALL of them are
  considered. Set tags on Submit to route each workflow's jobs to its own trigger.

Output: the raw IBM job object per fired job (status at `state.status`), plus three added keys
lifted from `state`: `reason`, `reasonCode` and `reasonSolution`. They are `null` when the job
did not fail, and IBM leaves them empty for cancellations. The job's own fields are untouched,
so `$json.id`, `$json.backend` and `$json.state` keep working.

`ibmQuantumErrorTrigger` is retired. It is marked `hidden`, so it no longer appears in the node
panel, but it stays registered and any saved workflow using it keeps polling unchanged. Do not
add it to new workflows; use `ibmQuantumTrigger` with `statusFilter: failedOrCanceled`, which
matches the same jobs and emits the same three reason fields. It is NOT a drop-in replacement
in a saved workflow, because the two nodes shape their output differently:

- the job ID is `jobId` here and `id` on the main trigger;
- `status` here is always lowercased by `extractJobStatus`, while the main trigger spreads IBM's
  job unchanged, so its `status` keeps IBM's casing (`Cancelled`, `Failed`) and is missing entirely
  if IBM omits the field;
- the raw job sits under `job` here and is spread across the top level on the main trigger.

`reason`, `reasonCode` and `reasonSolution` are identical on both. The payloads are deliberately
left alone, since changing either would break workflows already running on it. Its parameters
remain `errorFilter`
(options: `any` default meaning failed or canceled, `failed`, `canceled`), plus the same
`limit` and `tagFilter`.

Output per job: `{ jobId, backend, status, reason, reasonCode, reasonSolution, job }`, carrying the
failure reason IBM recorded (for example code 1517 for a non-ISA circuit), IBM's suggested solution,
and the full job body under `job`.

## Gate palette and OpenQASM 3 emission (Circuit Build)

Emitted program header: `OPENQASM 3.0;` then `include "stdgates.inc";` then, only when a row uses
`rzz`, Qiskit's block `gate rzz(p0) _gate_q_0, _gate_q_1 { cx _gate_q_0, _gate_q_1; rz(p0)
_gate_q_1; cx _gate_q_0, _gate_q_1; }` on five lines, then one `input float[64] name;` per circuit
parameter, then `qubit[n] q;` then `bit[m] c;` (the bit register only when `numClbits` is above 0).
The `input` declarations come BEFORE `qubit[n] q;`, never after the registers.

The palette addresses VIRTUAL qubits (`q[i]`), while Qiskit's exporter writes PHYSICAL qubits
(`$i`) and declares no register. IBM's OpenQASM 3 feature table
(https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/en/guides/qasm-feature-table) says that for execution on
hardware only circuits written in terms of hardware qubits, for example `$0`, are valid, and marks
custom `gate` definitions as not valid for hardware verbatim. In practice the virtual form runs
today: every live measurement in this file used it, IBM places `q[i]` on physical qubit `i`
unchanged (the `cz q[0], q[5]` that failed on ibm_fez was reported on qubits `(0, 5)`), and Qiskit's
own `gate rzz` block completed on the same device. IBM promises neither. When a job has to be
written the way IBM documents, submit the `$n` form: Qiskit's `qasm3.dumps` output, or by hand
`OPENQASM 3.0;` then `include "stdgates.inc";` then `bit[1] c;` then `x $0;` then
`c[0] = measure $0;`, one statement per line: the header every submit requires and the include that
defines `x` stay, only the `qubit` line goes. The submit warnings read `$n`, `q[n]` and any other
register name alike, so switching form loses no check. Keep one statement per line in either form:
the `rzz` and `id` checks only see what a line begins with, the ISA check takes one name per line
and on a line carrying an assignment reads only what follows the `=`, and the noise learner's
classical-register warning wants `bit[n]` at the start of a line, so a program squeezed onto a
single line keeps only the coupling check.

| gate value | qubit indices | params | emitted as | on IBM hardware |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `id` | 1 | 0 | NOTHING (validated, then dropped) | failed every job it was measured in (0.3.3): stdgates defines `id` as `U(0, 0, 0)` and IBM's importer most likely expands it, although IBM lists `id` as native; the no-op is omitted instead and `instructionCount` shows the drop |
| `x` | 1 | 0 | `x q[i];` | runs as-is |
| `sx` | 1 | 0 | `sx q[i];` | runs as-is |
| `y`, `z` | 1 | 0 | `y q[i];` etc. | transpile first |
| `h` | 1 | 0 | `h q[i];` | transpile first |
| `s`, `sdg`, `t`, `tdg` | 1 | 0 | `s q[i];` etc. | transpile first |
| `rx`, `rz` | 1 | 1 | `rx(angle) q[i];` | runs as-is |
| `ry`, `p` | 1 | 1 | `ry(angle) q[i];` | transpile first |
| `u` | 1 | 3 | `U(theta, phi, lambda) q[i];` (uppercase builtin; a lowercase `u` does not exist in stdgates and is rejected) | transpile first |
| `cz` | 2 (control,target) | 0 | `cz q[c], q[t];` | runs as-is |
| `rzz` | 2 | 1 | `rzz(angle) q[a], q[b];` with the `gate rzz` block in the header | runs as-is on Heron (fractional: angle in (0, pi/2], no Nighthawk, no gate twirling, no resilience level 2) |
| `cx` | 2 (control,target) | 0 | `cx q[c], q[t];` | transpile first |
| `swap` | 2 | 0 | `swap q[a], q[b];` | transpile first |
| `crx`, `cry`, `crz` | 2 (control,target) | 1 | `crx(angle) q[c], q[t];` | transpile first |
| `ccx` | 3 (control,control,target) | 0 | `ccx q[c1], q[c2], q[t];` | transpile first |
| `measure` | 1 | 0 (plus `clbit`) | `c[clbit] = measure q[i];` | runs as-is |
| `reset` | 1 | 0 | `reset q[i];` | runs as-is |
| `delay` | 1 | 0 (plus `duration`) | `delay[100ns] q[i];` | runs as-is |
| `barrier` | any (empty means all) | 0 | `barrier q[i], q[j];` or `barrier q;` | directive, always fine |

Angles are radians or declared parameter names. `rzz` is in the palette as of 0.6.0:
`stdgates.inc` has no definition for it, so a bare `rzz(0.5) q[0], q[1];` comes back Failed naming
`gate 'rzz' is not defined` (measured on ibm_fez; the reason code varies between 1506 and 1603,
match on the message), while the same call carrying Qiskit's own `gate rzz` block completed on the
same device; that run is recorded with the operand names `a, b`. The builder therefore writes that
definition once whenever a circuit uses `rzz`, in Qiskit 2.5.2's `_gate_q_0, _gate_q_1` spelling of
it: the operand names are local to the block. Submit still warns about a bare `rzz` in OpenQASM
supplied by hand. `delay` carries its duration in brackets and is a native instruction on every
device. Neither a `delay` nor an `input` declaration written by the palette has run on hardware from
this project yet; the `gate rzz` block has, hand-written, for 0.5.0.
`sx` IS in the palette as of 0.5.0. It was left out on the belief that it had no OpenQASM 3 spelling
avoiding the builtin `U`, which is wrong: `stdgates.inc` defines it, Qiskit's own exporter writes the
bare `sx q[i];` for a transpiled circuit, and IBM runs it. Verified on ibm_fez: two in a row read 249
of 256 shots as 1, which is X, and one alone reads a 47/53 split.

## Hardware reality: ISA circuits and transpilation

The single most common failure. The Qiskit Runtime REST API does NOT transpile. Real hardware
executes only its native gate set (on 2026-09-10 all three Heron devices this account reaches list
`cz, id, rx, rz, rzz, sx, x, xslow`, plus measure, reset, delay and barrier; IBM extends the list,
`xslow` was not there two days earlier, so check any backend with Backend Get Configuration, field
`basis_gates`) over a fixed
qubit topology. Submitting a non-ISA circuit (anything with `h`, `cx`, `u`, `ry` and so on) fails:

    reason_code 1517: The instruction h on qubits (0,) is not supported by the target system.
    Transpile your circuits for the target before submitting a primitive query.

That is hardware behaviour, not a node bug. A failed job still consumes quota. Three ways to get an
ISA circuit:

1. Build natively in the node. Gates safe on Heron QPUs (ibm_kingston, ibm_fez and ibm_marrakesh,
   the three the Open instance behind this file's measurements reached): `x`, `sx`, `rx`, `rz`,
   `rzz`, `cz`, `delay`, `reset`, `barrier`, `measure`. Two identities cover most needs (up to
   global phase):
   `H = rz(pi/2) sx rz(pi/2)` and `CNOT(c to t) = H(t) cz(c,t) H(t)`, with pi/2 =
   1.5707963267948966. A Bell state is 13 gate entries (see the example workflow below), verified on
   ibm_fez at 2048 shots: 48.7% `00` and 46.2% `11`, the rest readout error. Prefer `sx` over a
   parametrised `rx` in that identity. Both work on Heron, but `rx(pi/2)` is a fractional gate, and
   on Nighthawk r1 processors (ibm_miami in us-east, ibm_berlin in eu-de) the basis is
   `cz, id, rz, sx, x` with no fractional `rx` at all, so the `sx` form runs on both fleets while the
   `rx` form does not. Adjacency matters as much as the gate set: a two-qubit gate must land on a
   pair the device couples. On submit, the node reads `coupling_map` from the backend configuration
   and warns about the pairs that are not in it, naming the qubits and the neighbours the first one
   does have; past the twentieth distinct pair one closing sentence counts the rest instead of
   naming them. The check reads `$n` physical qubits as well as `q[n]`, so it also covers the
   transpiled string from point 2 below. Verified on ibm_fez: `cz q[0], q[5]` is accepted by IBM,
   queued, and then failed with code 1517, "the instruction cz on qubits (0, 5) is not supported by
   the target system", while `cz q[0], q[1]` completes. The check shares one GET per submit with
   the ISA check, which reads `basis_gates` and `supported_instructions` from the same response; the
   GET is made for every OpenQASM 3 submit, is skipped for QPY, and never blocks a submit: if the
   configuration cannot be read the coupling check is silent and the ISA check falls back to the
   Heron union. Fractional gates are also incompatible with gate twirling and with ZNE and PEC
   error mitigation, so avoid Estimator resilience level 2 on circuits containing a parametrised
   `rx`.
2. Transpile locally with Qiskit (free, any plan, no live credentials needed):
   `generate_preset_pass_manager(optimization_level=1, backend=FakeFez()).run(qc)` then
   `qiskit.qasm3.dumps(isa)`, and paste or pipe the string into the node. Pin the SAME backend on
   Submit that you transpiled for, because an ISA circuit is topology-specific. Transpile against
   the backend (or its `target`), not against a bare `basis_gates` list with the coupling map: the
   list carries no angle range, so Qiskit folds `rzz` angles freely and writes calls such as
   `rzz(-pi/2)` that IBM's fractional `rzz` refuses with code 1517, measured on `ibm_marrakesh` on
   2026-09-10 with a Grover circuit and a QFT; the node warns about such a call before the job goes
   out. For the Estimator, lay the observables out on the transpiled circuit as well,
   `observable.apply_layout(isa.layout)`: a four-qubit ansatz that transpilation spread over five
   physical qubits failed with code 1501, "The number of qubits of the circuit (5) does not match
   the number of qubits of the (0,)-th observable (4)", measured the same day. A QPY circuit keeps
   every qubit of the device it was transpiled for, 156 on a Heron, so its observables must be laid
   out to that full width: a two-qubit `ZZ` sent with a QPY Bell state failed with the same code.
   Every submit check reads OpenQASM 3 text; a QPY circuit is opaque to all of them, so it draws no
   warning and IBM's refusal is the first signal, as it was for a QPY circuit carrying `rx` sent to
   the noise learner, code 1519, both measured on 2026-09-10. If the circuit uses
   anything OpenQASM 3 cannot express, dump it as QPY instead and submit with `circuitFormat: qpy`.
3. IBM's AI-powered transpiler passes, from the `qiskit-ibm-transpiler` package (beta). They are a
   local drop-in for the preset passes in step 2, not a cloud service: in IBM's words the passes run
   on your local environment, with models downloaded from Hugging Face. The former cloud Qiskit
   Transpiler Service REST API is gone (its guide answers 410, its host no longer resolves, and the
   package's 0.14.0 notes record the migration to Qiskit Functions), so there is nothing for this
   node to call and no plan requirement for transpiling. The result is an ISA circuit submitted like
   any other.

The fleet IBM lists as of September 2026, by processor family: Heron r2 ibm_kingston (the device
IBM names as available to every Open Plan user), ibm_fez and ibm_marrakesh; Heron r3 ibm_boston and
ibm_pittsburgh (us-east) and ibm_aachen (eu-de); Nighthawk r1 ibm_miami (us-east) and ibm_berlin
(eu-de); Nighthawk r2 ibm_phoenix (September 2026, Premium, Flex and Pay-As-You-Go), whose basis IBM
has not published, so read `basis_gates` with Backend Get Configuration before building for it.
Retired, and no longer valid as a `backend` value: ibm_torino (1 April 2026), ibm_strasbourg and
ibm_brussels (27 April 2026), ibm_brisbane (3 November 2025), ibm_sherbrooke (31 July 2025),
ibm_kyiv (18 April 2025); every Eagle device is gone. Backend Get Many is the authority for what a
given instance can reach.

There is no simulator to fall back on: IBM retired its cloud simulators on 15 May 2024 and marks
`is_simulator` deprecated, so every job runs on hardware and needs an ISA circuit.
`includeSimulators` on Get Least Busy stays for saved workflows and finds nothing.

## Results format and bit order (Job Get Results)

While the job is not finished, the node polls GET /jobs/{id} every `pollInterval` seconds until a
terminal status or `maxWait`, with `exclude_params=true` on every poll, so the `job` body in the
outcomes below never carries `params` (the submitted circuit); `getStatus` returns it. Outcomes:

- Timed out: `{ jobId, status, timedOut: true, job }`. The job may still be running; the jobId stays
  valid, so re-check later or use the trigger.
- Terminal but not completed (failed or cancelled): `{ jobId, status, reason, reasonCode,
  reasonSolution, job }`. The three reason fields are lifted out of `job.state` so the cause is
  readable without digging; they are null when IBM supplies none, as it does for a cancel. Failure details
  at `job.state.reason`, `reason_code` and `reason_solution`.
- Completed: `{ jobId, status: "completed", pubCount, pubs, resultsAvailable?, resultsUnreadable?,
  registerError?, raw }`. `resultsAvailable: false` appears when the result body is empty, and only
  then. That is the 204 IBM documents as "Job's final result not found", which the transport turns
  into `{}` and which without the flag looks identical to a completed job that produced zero pubs.
  A body that carries content the node cannot read is not flagged: it comes back with `pubCount: 0`
  and the body untouched in `raw`, which is where a shape the reader does not know has always been
  readable. A string body that is not the serialised encoding, which is the `LegacyJobResults`
  branch of IBM's own results schema, and a `results` key that is not an array both land there, so
  read `raw` whenever `pubCount` is 0 rather than only when the flag is set.
  `resultsUnreadable` appears only for a serialised body that is not valid JSON, and carries the
  reason; the text stays in `raw`. `registerError` appears only for a `registerName` no pub carries,
  and is described below the pub shapes. An entry inside `results` that is not an object reads as an
  empty pub rather than failing the item, so a body the node cannot read still reaches the workflow
  whole in `raw`.

Each entry in `pubs`:
- Sampler: `{ type: "sampler", register, numBits, shots, counts, metadata, requestedRegister?,
  registerFallback?, unparsedSamples? }`.
  `counts` maps bitstrings to occurrence counts, e.g. `{ "00": 512, "11": 498 }`. Bit order follows
  the classical register: **c[0] is the RIGHTMOST bit** (the standard Qiskit convention). Samples
  arrive as hex and are decoded with BigInt, so registers wider than 53 bits stay exact.
  `unparsedSamples` appears only when some samples could not be parsed, which is what explains a
  counts total below shots.
- Estimator: `{ type: "estimator", evs, stds, ensembleStandardError, metadata }`, the expectation
  value or values matching the observables submitted.
- Either primitive in the serialised Qiskit encoding, marked by
  `encoding: "qiskit-serialized"`. IBM picks the encoding from the submitted params, not from the
  endpoint: without `support_qiskit` the body is the plain JSON above, and with it, which is what
  `qiskit-ibm-runtime` sends by default, the body is a serialised object graph carrying no
  `results` key. A job submitted from Qiskit and read here arrives that way. A sampler PUB is
  `{ type: "sampler", encoding, register, numBits, samplesEncoded, requestedRegister?,
  registerFallback?, metadata }` and an estimator PUB is `{ type: "estimator", encoding,
  fieldNames, fieldsEncoded, metadata }`, where `fieldsEncoded` maps each name in `fieldNames` to
  its array. `samplesEncoded` and every value in `fieldsEncoded` are base64 of a zlib-compressed
  NumPy array, passed through undecoded for the same reason `ratesEncoded` is: `zlib` is not on the
  community-node import allowlist. Decode them with `zlib.inflate` outside n8n, or hand them to
  `qiskit-ibm-runtime`. Branch on `encoding` rather than on the absence of `counts`.
- Noise learner: `{ type: "noiseLearner", qubits, generators, ratesEncoded, circuitEncoded }`, one
  entry per learned layer. This primitive answers on a different shape: its payload arrives under
  `data` rather than `results`, so it has no PUBs and no classical registers, and `registerName` is
  ignored for it. `generators` is the plain Pauli list, e.g. `["IX", "IY", ..., "ZZ"]`, and
  `ratesEncoded` holds one rate per generator in the same order, as base64 of a zlib-compressed
  NumPy float64 array. It is passed through rather than decoded, because inflating it needs `zlib`,
  which the community-node import allowlist does not permit. `circuitEncoded` is the layer as QPY,
  passed through for the same reason. Both decode with `zlib.inflate` outside n8n, or by handing the
  raw value to qiskit-ibm-runtime. The full body stays in `raw`.
- Noise learner in IBM's older array encoding, marked by `encoding: "ibm-array"`:
  `{ type: "noiseLearner", encoding, numQubits, generatorsSparse, ratesEncoded, ratesShape,
  ratesStdEncoded, metadata }`, again one entry per learned layer. `generatorsSparse` is the sparse
  spelling of the same Pauli list, one entry per generator, each `[[label, [qubit, ...]], ...]`, so
  `[["XX", [0, 1]]]` is `XX` on qubits 0 and 1. `ratesEncoded` and `ratesStdEncoded` are base64 of a
  raw little-endian float64 buffer, one value per generator in the generator order, NOT compressed:
  `ratesShape` gives the element count and the buffer is exactly eight bytes per element, so
  `Buffer.from(ratesEncoded, "base64")` read as a Float64Array decodes it inside n8n with no `zlib`
  and no external step. `ratesStdEncoded` carries the same shape. Every layer measured declares
  `f64`; the dtype IBM sent is in `raw` under `data[i].rates.dtype` if that ever changes.
- Executor: `{ type: "executor", encoding: "ibm-array", registers, metadata }`, one entry per
  execution unit, for jobs run through IBM's Executor program. This node does not submit that
  program; the shape is here because Get Results reads any job id the account can see, including one
  a Qiskit session submitted. `registers` maps each register name IBM returned, such as `meas`,
  `measurement_flips.meas` and `pauli_signs`, to `{ encoded, shape, dtype }`, where `encoded` is
  base64 of the raw buffer and `shape` and `dtype` are IBM's own, typically a `bool` array of
  `[shots, slots, bits]`. Nothing is compressed, but a `bool` array is bit-packed over the flattened
  array, eight values to a byte, the way `numpy.packbits` writes it: `[256, 64, 15]` is 245760
  values in 30720 bytes, measured. Unpack it before reading, and do not assume one byte per element.
  There are no counts and no classical register parsing on this shape, and `registerName` is ignored
  for it, as it is for the noise learner.

`raw` is the untouched IBM response if deeper fields are needed. `registerName` forces reading a
specific classical register when a circuit defines several. Leave it empty to auto-detect. If the
named register is not in the result the item carries `registerError`, the sentence naming it and
listing the registers that are, and the counts still come back: the body has been downloaded by the
time the name is judged, and IBM deletes a private job's results once they have been read, so
failing the item would destroy the only copy of the shots. No other register's counts ever come back
under the name you asked for: a pub that lacks it reads its own register and marks that with
`registerFallback: true` and `requestedRegister`. A job can hold several pubs whose circuits name
their registers differently, so `registerError` appears only when NO pub carries the name, while a
name some pub carries leaves the item clean and marks only the pubs that fell back. Branch on
`registerError` where a wrong Register Name must stop the workflow. In the serialised encoding the
names compared against are the PUB field names, so a Register Name set on an estimator result
reports against `evs`, `stds` and the rest; in the plain encoding only registers carrying samples
count, so an estimator result ignores the name entirely.

## Error handling

- IBM error bodies (`{ errors: [{ code, message, solution }] }`) are unwrapped: the real message
  becomes the n8n error message and IBM's `solution` becomes the description, instead of a generic
  "Bad request".
- With "Continue on Fail" enabled, failed items yield `{ error: "<message>" }` and the run continues.
- With it off the run stops on the first failure, and the error carries the index of the input item
  that caused it, an error from IBM as much as a local one, so n8n can point at that item.
- Local validation fails BEFORE any request, and before any quota is spent, for: malformed gate
  input, a circuit that is not OpenQASM 3 (or not QPY when that format is selected), invalid Pauli
  observables, non-object Additional Options, an Additional Options top-level key outside the
  program's schema, invalid register sizes, a switch an expression left as something other than true
  or false, and a malformed API version.
- Every HTTP request has a 30-second timeout. Numeric fields bypassed by expressions are either
  clamped or refused. Clamped: shots and limits fall back to defaults, Job Get Many caps at 200 per
  request and at 50 pages with Return All, Workload Get Many at 50 per request and at 20 pages,
  trigger "Jobs to Scan" at 200, the job cost at 10800, and the three noise learning counts in
  Resilience Options are dropped at zero. Refused with an error naming the parameter: `minQubits`,
  `resilienceLevel` (integer 0 to 2), `precision` and `defaultPrecision` (number at least 0),
  `seedEstimator` (integer 0 to 2147483647), the twirling counts (integer at least 1 or `auto`),
  `repDelay` and `pecMaxOverhead` (number at least 0), `pecNoiseGain` (number at least 0 or `auto`),
  `zneNoiseFactors` (finite numbers), `noiseLearningLayerPairDepths` (whole numbers),
  `instanceLimit` (an integer of at least 1 unless `clearLimit` is on), a `rankBy` or
  `processorFamily` outside its accepted form, an `updatedBefore` that is not a date, a gate
  `duration` that is not a number followed by a unit, a gate angle naming a parameter that
  `circuitParameters` did not declare, and register sizes. The fields read as text
  (`seedEstimator`, the twirling counts, `pecNoiseGain`, `zneNoiseFactors` and
  `noiseLearningLayerPairDepths`) check text and numbers, and the two comma-separated lists also
  read an array of numbers. A value an expression hands over that is neither text nor a number, such
  as null, a boolean or an object, is refused by the twirling counts and `pecNoiseGain`, and omits
  the key for `seedEstimator`, `zneNoiseFactors` and `noiseLearningLayerPairDepths`. An expression
  that resolves to nothing is the exception: it reaches the node as `undefined`, which is how an
  entry that was never added reads, so it omits the key for all five.
- Every switch the node reads is read the same way, whether it sits on its own or inside a
  collection: `includeSimulators`, `dynamicalDecoupling`, `twirlingGates`, `twirlingMeasure`,
  `privateJob`, `includeParams` (the Get Status field and the Get Many filter), `returnAll` on all
  three listings, `acceptingJobs`, `clearLimit`, `skipResetQubits`, `initQubits`,
  `measureMitigation`, `zneMitigation`, `pecMitigation` and the `simulators` analytics filter. The
  boolean itself is taken as it is; the text `true` and `false` in any case and with surrounding
  spaces, and 1 and 0 as text or as a number, are read as the switch they spell; null, undefined and
  an empty or blank string keep the field's own default, and leave the key out of the request for
  the five flags inside the option collections and for the `simulators` analytics filter; anything
  else, `'yes'`, `'off'`, 2, an array or an object, is refused before the request with `<Field> must
  be true or false. An expression may also hand over "true", "false", 1 or 0.` So a Dynamical
  Decoupling of `'false'` sends no `dynamical_decoupling.enable`, a Private of `'true'` marks the
  job private, and a Return All of `'true'` pages. An `options` parameter an expression leaves null,
  undefined or an empty string falls back to its own default where the field checks for the empty
  value (`rankBy`, `processorFamily` and the `plan` filter on Get Many Instances); everywhere else
  read the parameter's own row, since a null `groupBy` on Get Usage Analytics Grouped and a null
  Session Mode on Session Create travel to IBM as null, and a null `gate` or `resilienceLevel` is
  refused before any request.
- A non-empty value outside the accepted list is refused where the operation checks membership:
