  `rankBy` and the `plan` filter on Get Many Instances name the accepted values in the error, the
  palette's `gate` fails with `Unsupported gate: <name>`, `resilienceLevel` is caught by the
  bounded-number guard above, and an unknown `resource` or `operation` fails locally with an
  `Unsupported ...` message naming the value. `processorFamily` refuses a value that is neither
  text nor a number and uses a number as the family name, so a family outside IBM's list matches no
  device and returns `leastBusy: null`. Nothing else on the request path checks membership, so the
  choices inside the primitive option collections reach IBM exactly as written, and the `pending`
  and `sort` job filters are dropped when the value is not one of theirs.
- Required identifiers (`jobId`, `sessionId`, `backendName`, submit `backend`, session `backend`)
  are refused when empty. A bare `/jobs/` is answered by IBM with its web app, so an empty Job ID
  used to return 285 KB of HTML as a successful job status.
- Every identifier is URL-encoded before it becomes a path segment, so a value like `../backends`
  cannot redirect the request to a different endpoint.
- No refusal repeats what a credential field holds. A malformed `apiVersion` fails with `The
  credential's API Version is not a YYYY-MM-DD date. Use 2026-04-15.` The prefix check on the CRN
  belongs to `setCostLimit`, the one operation that puts a CRN in a path: the credential's value, or
  this operation's own `instanceCrn` parameter when that is set, fails there with `Instance CRN does
  not start with crn:v1:. Copy the full CRN from the IBM Quantum Platform instances page.` A
  malformed account segment fails in `getAccountConfiguration`, the one operation that reads the
  account id out of the CRN, with `The account id in the credential's Instance CRN is not one IBM
  accepts: letters, digits, - and _ only, at most 64 characters.` No other operation reads the CRN
  locally: the credential puts it on the `Service-CRN` header of each authenticated request. The
  reason for not quoting is the mis-paste: those boxes take strings as opaque as the API key, and a
  quoted value would reach the output item, the saved execution and an AI tool's context in
  plaintext. The two messages that do name a credential value name one the check in front of them
  has already proved harmless: the deprecation warning names a version proved to be a date, and the
  shared identifier guard names a value of nothing but dots. This covers the messages the node
  writes, not IBM's, which are relayed word for word: the `code 1279` above names the `Service-CRN`
  header it was sent, measured with a well formed CRN of the wrong region. What IBM answers for a
  value that is not a CRN at all has not been observed, and its registry also carries `1241`
  "Invalid CRN." and `1348` "Invalid CRN format. The CRN must have the expected number of fields.",
  whose text has no room for the value. Rotate a key that has been in that box either way:
  `instanceCrn` is not a password field, so it is shown in cleartext in the credential form and
  goes to IBM on every authenticated request.
- `jobTags` is bounded locally to IBM's schema: at most 8 tags, each at most 86 characters. Text, a
  number and an array all read as a tag list, and an empty value clears the job's tags on purpose;
  anything else is refused, and so is any array entry that is blank or is neither text nor a number,
  with the position of that entry named, because Update Tags PUTs the whole list and an entry
  dropped for being unreadable is a tag deleted from the job. The guard reads array entries only:
  comma-separated text still drops its empty entries, so a value of nothing but separators clears
  the job.
- `calibrationId` and `submitCalibrationId` are bounded locally to IBM's schema, at most 100
  characters; an empty value omits the parameter. `updatedBefore` is refused before the request
  unless it parses as a date and time.
- `submitSessionId` is bounded locally to IBM's schema: at most 36 characters, the length of the
  UUIDs Session Create returns; a longer value is refused before any request.

Common failures. IBM's error registry, https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/en/errors, defines every
code (383 of them); the quoted message text below is IBM's own, and the fix column is shortened
from IBM's solution text:

| symptom | cause and fix |
| :-- | :-- |
| 401 or IAM token errors | API key wrong, revoked or expired; regenerate it at cloud.ibm.com/iam/apikeys |
| 404 or empty backends list, `code 1279` "Instance crn:... not found" | credential `region` does not match the instance CRN's region. Authentication is fine; only the instance is regional. `getApiVersions` still works, because `/versions` is not instance-scoped |
| job fails, reason_code 1517, "Circuits do not match the target definition (non-ISA circuits)" | circuit not ISA for that backend (the live `reason` text instead names the instruction and qubits); transpile or build natively |
| job fails, reason_code 1506, "QASM parsing failed" | the OpenQASM 3 text does not import into Qiskit: an undefined gate (a bare `rzz`), a lowercase `u`, a syntax slip. The same bad program draws 1506 on one submission and 1603 on the next, so match on the message, never on the code |
| job fails, reason_code 1603, "Error loading QASM circuit with the standard Qiskit loaders" | the same causes as 1506, plus duplicate operands (`cx q[0], q[0]`) and base64 QPY that was not zlib-compressed; Circuit Build refuses a repeated index and Submit refuses uncompressed QPY, both before the request |
| job fails, reason_code 1519, "One or more circuits contain fractional gates, which cannot be used with the given options or other circuit instructions" | `twirlingGates` on, `pecMitigation` on in Resilience Options, or `zneAmplifier` set to `pea` there (Estimator `resilienceLevel` 2 turns gate twirling on), with a parametrised `rx` or `rzz` in the circuit; turn the option off or remove the fractional gates |
| job fails, reason_code 1520, "Circuits or PUBs exceed one or more system limits" | over an IBM limit: 10 million Sampler executions per job, 30 million `rz`, 20 million `sx` or 5 million two-qubit gates per circuit, 26.8 million control-system instructions per qubit; split the work into several jobs |
| job fails, reason_code 1521, "Incompatible circuits and/or options specified" | an options combination IBM rejects; the message names it, and the registry entry links IBM's options compatibility page |
| job fails, reason_code 1522, "Dynamic circuits used in a V2 Estimator job" | control flow (an `if` on a measured bit) sent to `submitEstimator`; the V2 Estimator does not support it, so use `submitSampler` or drop the control flow |
| job fails, reason_code 1501, "The number of qubits of the circuit (N) does not match the number of qubits of the observable (M)" | observables written for the logical circuit, sent with a transpiled one that spans more physical qubits; apply the transpiled layout to the observables (`apply_layout`) or transpile onto a contiguous set (measured 2026-09-10) |
| job fails, reason_code 1217, "Session has been closed" | the job was still queued in a session when Session Close ran; Close cancels queued work rather than draining it, so set Accepting Jobs to false and wait for the queue first (measured 2026-09-10) |
| submit fails, code 5302, "Failed to publish job: maximum payload exceeded" | the job body is too large. IBM publishes no byte figure; its remedy is fewer shots per job (under 10000) with the results stitched together, or fewer circuits per job |
| Session Create fails, code 1352, "You are not authorized to run a session when using the {} plan" | `dedicated` on an Open instance; use `batch`, or a paid plan |
| "gate twirling does not support fractional gates" | `twirlingGates` on with a parametrised rx or rzz; turn it off. This is the live `reason` text of the 1519 family above |
| Estimator submit rejected | observables length does not match the qubit count, or invalid Pauli letters |
| Get Results returns timedOut | hardware queue exceeded `maxWait`; raise it, or use the trigger pattern |
| "is not a YYYY-MM-DD date" | the credential's API Version field is malformed; set it to 2026-04-15 |

## Recommended workflow patterns

1. Quick run (short queues): Circuit Build, then Backend Get Least Busy, then Job
   Submit to Sampler, then Job Get Results. Get Results blocks the execution while polling, which is
   fine for minutes and fragile for hours.
2. Production run (real hardware, long queues), splitting submission from results:
   - Workflow A: build and submit with `jobTags` set (for example `my-experiment`), finishing at once.
   - Workflow B (ACTIVE): IBM Quantum Trigger with the same tag in `tagFilter` and statusFilter
     `completed`, then Job Get Results (which returns instantly, the job being already done).
   - Workflow C (ACTIVE): IBM Quantum Trigger with the same tag and statusFilter
     `failedOrCanceled`, for alerting or a fallback, using `reason`, `reasonCode` and
     `reasonSolution`.
3. Iterative loops (VQE, QAOA): Session Create (mode `batch` on the free plan), then repeated
   Submits with `submitSessionId` and `parameters` bindings, then Session Close. Check Account Get
   Usage first, and consider `maxCost` on each submit.
4. Quota reporting and capping: Schedule Trigger, then Account Get Usage Analytics Grouped by
   backend or plan, for a periodic spend report; Account Get Many Instances for every instance's
   cap, allocation and allowed backends in one call, Account Get Account Configuration for the
   plan-level limits, and Account Set Cost Limit to cap one instance before a large run. The reads
   consume no QPU time.
5. AI agent: attach the ACTION node to an n8n AI Agent as a tool for the read paths (least busy
   backend, job status, usage). Pair submission with a pre-built ISA circuit.

## Example workflow JSON

A complete, runnable n8n workflow: a hardware-safe Bell state (native gates only, no transpiler), a
least-busy backend, submit, then a blocking wait for counts. Replace the credential id and name with
the user's own. On import, n8n rewires everything from this JSON.

```json
{
  "name": "IBM Quantum Bell state",
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "m1", "name": "Run", "type": "n8n-nodes-base.manualTrigger", "typeVersion": 1, "position": [0, 0], "parameters": {} },
    { "id": "c1", "name": "Build Bell (ISA)", "type": "n8n-nodes-ibm-quantum.ibmQuantum", "typeVersion": 2, "position": [200, 0],
      "credentials": { "ibmQuantumApi": { "id": "REPLACE_ME", "name": "IBM Quantum account" } },
      "parameters": { "resource": "circuit", "operation": "build", "numQubits": 2, "numClbits": 2,
        "gates": { "gate": [
          { "gate": "rz", "qubits": "0", "params": "1.5707963267948966" },
          { "gate": "sx", "qubits": "0" },
          { "gate": "rz", "qubits": "0", "params": "1.5707963267948966" },
          { "gate": "rz", "qubits": "1", "params": "1.5707963267948966" },
          { "gate": "sx", "qubits": "1" },
          { "gate": "rz", "qubits": "1", "params": "1.5707963267948966" },
          { "gate": "cz", "qubits": "0,1" },
          { "gate": "rz", "qubits": "1", "params": "1.5707963267948966" },
          { "gate": "sx", "qubits": "1" },
          { "gate": "rz", "qubits": "1", "params": "1.5707963267948966" },
          { "gate": "barrier", "qubits": "0,1" },
          { "gate": "measure", "qubits": "0", "clbit": 0 },
          { "gate": "measure", "qubits": "1", "clbit": 1 }
        ] } } },
    { "id": "b1", "name": "Least Busy QPU", "type": "n8n-nodes-ibm-quantum.ibmQuantum", "typeVersion": 2, "position": [400, 0],
      "credentials": { "ibmQuantumApi": { "id": "REPLACE_ME", "name": "IBM Quantum account" } },
      "parameters": { "resource": "backend", "operation": "getLeastBusy", "minQubits": 2, "includeSimulators": false } },
    { "id": "j1", "name": "Submit", "type": "n8n-nodes-ibm-quantum.ibmQuantum", "typeVersion": 2, "position": [600, 0],
      "credentials": { "ibmQuantumApi": { "id": "REPLACE_ME", "name": "IBM Quantum account" } },
      "parameters": { "resource": "job", "operation": "submitSampler",
        "backend": "={{ $json.leastBusy }}",
        "circuitFormat": "qasm3",
        "qasm3": "={{ $('Build Bell (ISA)').item.json.qasm3 }}",
        "shots": 1024, "maxCost": 60, "jobTags": "bell-demo" } },
    { "id": "j2", "name": "Get Results", "type": "n8n-nodes-ibm-quantum.ibmQuantum", "typeVersion": 2, "position": [800, 0],
      "credentials": { "ibmQuantumApi": { "id": "REPLACE_ME", "name": "IBM Quantum account" } },
      "parameters": { "resource": "job", "operation": "getResults",
        "jobId": "={{ $json.jobId }}", "pollInterval": 5, "maxWait": 600 } }
  ],
  "connections": {
    "Run": { "main": [[{ "node": "Build Bell (ISA)", "type": "main", "index": 0 }]] },
    "Build Bell (ISA)": { "main": [[{ "node": "Least Busy QPU", "type": "main", "index": 0 }]] },
    "Least Busy QPU": { "main": [[{ "node": "Submit", "type": "main", "index": 0 }]] },
    "Submit": { "main": [[{ "node": "Get Results", "type": "main", "index": 0 }]] }
  }
}
```

Expected counts: mostly `00` and `11` in near-equal parts, with a few percent of `01` and `10` from
readout noise. The `cz` between qubits 0 and 1 assumes those qubits are coupled, which holds on
current IBM devices; for full generality transpile for the exact backend instead of using Get Least
Busy.

## Using the node as an AI Agent tool

The action node sets `usableAsTool`, so it can be attached to n8n's AI Agent node as a tool. The
good tool calls are the READ paths: Backend Get Least Busy ("which QPU has the shortest queue?", or
with `rankBy` and `processorFamily`, "which Heron device starts my job soonest?"), Account Get
Usage ("how much runtime is left?"), Account Get Account Configuration ("which backends
and session limits does my plan allow?"), Job Get Status (with `includeParams: false` the reply is
the state alone), Job Get Many, Workload Get Many. Parameters
can be delegated to the model with `$fromAI()` expressions, for example
`={{ $fromAI('jobId', 'the IBM Quantum job id') }}`. Submission as a tool works, but the model must
supply an ISA circuit, so pair it with a pre-built circuit rather than asking the model to write
QASM for hardware. Attach the ACTION node only; the triggers are not tools.

No environment variable gates tool usage. `N8N_COMMUNITY_PACKAGES_ALLOW_TOOL_USAGE` was removed in
n8n 1.85.0 (March 2025), which turned tool usage on for every community node; do not tell users to
set it. The variables n8n reads as of 2.37 concern community packages as a whole:
`N8N_COMMUNITY_PACKAGES_ENABLED` (default true; false disables verified and unverified packages
alike), `N8N_VERIFIED_PACKAGES_ENABLED` (default true), `N8N_UNVERIFIED_PACKAGES_ENABLED` (default
true, false from n8n 3.0), `N8N_COMMUNITY_PACKAGES_PREVENT_LOADING` (default false),
`N8N_COMMUNITY_PACKAGES_REGISTRY`, `N8N_COMMUNITY_PACKAGES_AUTH_TOKEN`, and since n8n 2.21.0
`N8N_COMMUNITY_PACKAGES_MANAGED_BY_ENV` with `N8N_COMMUNITY_PACKAGES`. This package is verified, so
the n8n 3.0 default change does not affect it. n8n verifies each release separately: a version newer
than the latest one n8n lists as verified counts as unverified until the listing catches up.
Reference: https://docs.n8n.io/deploy/host-n8n/configure-n8n/basic-configuration/use-environment-variables/nodes

## Limits, quotas and plan notes

- Open (free) plan: 10 minutes (600 seconds) of QPU time per 28-day rolling window; `batch` sessions
  only, never `dedicated` (error 1352), and a batch lives at most 10 minutes; failed jobs still
  consume quota; instances are us-east only. Since 16 March 2026 active Open Plan users can opt in
  to an additional 180 minutes over the following 12 months; IBM's plans page states no other
  condition.
- Plans are Open, Pay-As-You-Go, Flex, Premium and On-Prem.
- IBM rate-limits job submission to 5 jobs per minute per user. A single job may use at most 3
  hours (10800 seconds) of QPU time, Sampler jobs are capped at 10 million total executions, and
  per circuit IBM allows 30 million `rz`, 20 million `sx` and 5 million two-qubit gates within 26.8
  million control-system instructions per qubit (reason code 1520 when exceeded). IBM publishes no
  payload size in bytes; an oversized job body is refused with code 5302, and the documented remedy
  is fewer shots per job, stitched together afterwards.
- GET /jobs is capped at 200 results per call and GET /workloads at 50; the node clamps both.
  Return All walks past the first page: 50 pages of 200 on Job Get Many, 20 pages of 50 on
  Workload Get Many, and 20 pages of 100 on Account Get Many Instances. The two Qiskit Runtime
  listings add `truncated: true` only when the page cap, rather than the server, ended the walk;
  Get Many Instances always carries `truncated`, false when the listing was exhausted.
- Tags: at most 8 per job or filter.
- Up to 100 circuits per submitted job, the node's own bound rather than IBM's, one PUB each,
  sharing the same `shots`, `parameters`, `observables` and `precision`. Batching pays the roughly
  two second per job overhead once instead of once per circuit. To run many parameter sets, pass
  an array of circuits, use `parameters` bindings with arrays, or several Submits in a session.
- Every request times out after 30 seconds, so a hung connection cannot stall an execution.
- Get Results poll values are clamped to at least 1 second; defaults are a 5 second interval and a
  300 second maximum wait.
- Get Results polls with `exclude_params=true`, like the triggers, so the circuit payload is never
  re-downloaded while waiting.
- IBM exposes no push or webhook for job completion (verified against the API), so polling is the
  only mechanism, which is why the triggers exist.
- Job data is retained for 3 years.

## What this package does NOT do

- No transpilation. The REST API has none; transpile locally or build natively.
- No simulator of any kind: the node has no local one, and IBM retired its cloud simulators on
  15 May 2024, so every job runs on real hardware.
- No Executor, NoiseLearnerV3 or Calibrator programs. All three live on the same `POST /v1/jobs`
  endpoint the node already uses, but each requires circuits encoded as base64 QPY produced by
  Qiskit, which defeats the point of a package with no Qiskit dependency. The version 2 Noise
  Learner is supported precisely because it accepts a plain QASM string. The Executor and
  NoiseLearnerV3 results carry their own schemas too (`schema_version` on both, and
  `generators_sparse`, `num_qubits`, `rates` and `rates_std` under `data` on NoiseLearnerV3), which
  Get Results would report as noise learner pubs of nulls if it ever read such a job submitted from
  Python, because the parser recognises a body with `data` and no `results` as the version 2 learner
  shape. The untouched body is always there under `raw`.
- No instance creation, deletion or backend allowlist changes. IBM Cloud's Resource Controller
  offers all three on the same endpoint family; the node lists instances and writes one field, the
  cost limit.
- Three job and listing details are deliberately not exposed: `runtime` on `POST /jobs`, the
  `Parent-Job-Id` header, and `user=me` on `GET /workloads`. Each is niche, and none is needed for
  anything the node does today.
- No Qiskit Functions catalog or Qiskit Serverless endpoints. The cloud Qiskit Transpiler Service no
  longer exists, so there is nothing to wire in; its successor is a local Qiskit plugin (see
  "Hardware reality").
- No support for the retired legacy IBM Quantum platform or its token auth.
- No streaming or webhooks; job completion is detected by polling.

## Underlying REST API details (for debugging)

Base URL: `https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/api/v1` (us-east) or
`https://eu-de.quantum.cloud.ibm.com/api/v1` (eu-de). Headers on every call: `Authorization:
Bearer <IAM token>`, `Service-CRN: <instance CRN>`, `IBM-API-Version: <date>`. Endpoints used:
`GET /backends` (Get Least Busy adds `fields=wait_time_seconds`),
`GET /backends/{name}/configuration|properties|status|defaults` (with the optional
query parameters `calibration_id` on configuration and properties, and `updated_before` on
properties), `POST /jobs`, `GET /jobs`, `GET /jobs/{id}` (with `exclude_params` from Get Status's
toggle, and always true from the Get Results poll), `GET /jobs/{id}/results|logs|metrics`,
`PUT /jobs/{id}/tags`, `POST /jobs/{id}/cancel`, `DELETE /jobs/{id}`, `GET /workloads`,
`GET /tags`, `GET /versions`, `POST /sessions`, `GET /sessions/{id}`, `PATCH /sessions/{id}`,
`DELETE /sessions/{id}/close`, `GET /instance`,
`GET /instances/usage`, `GET /instances/configuration`, `GET /accounts/{id}`,
`GET /analytics/usage`, `GET /analytics/usage_grouped`, `GET /analytics/usage_grouped_by_date`,
`GET /analytics/filters`. Two account operations use a fourth host, IBM Cloud's Resource
Controller at `https://resource-controller.cloud.ibm.com`, with the same bearer token:
`GET /v2/resource_instances?resource_id=b6049020-80f4-11eb-a0f7-e35ec9b4054f` (paged by the
`start` token in `next_url`, page size up to 100, the cap this node applies; IBM's guide and its
SDK state no range for that parameter) and `PATCH /v2/resource_instances/{crn}` with the CRN
percent-encoded as one path segment. Guide:
https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/en/guides/access-instances-platform-apis
Array query parameters are sent as repeated keys (`tags=a&tags=b`);
bracket encodings are silently ignored by IBM. Official API reference:
https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/en/api/qiskit-runtime-rest
